title: Dental calculus examination for forensic and anthropological purposes
protocol: Sample two 3–5-mm-long fragments of dentin carious deposit directly from the teeth at the lingual position of mandibular premolar or molar with sterile surgical instruments.
Deposit the samples in a sterile box without any conservative agent.
Clean the samples by fine scraping with non-contaminating plastic instruments.
Vaporize pressured air on all faces of the samples for 10 minutes.
Conduct environmental scanning electron microscope examination using a Philips XL30 CP with X-ray micro-analysis (energy-dispersive X-ray spectroscopy).
Store images at a standard resolution digital frame store.
Perform a study with an optical microscope on other samples of dentin carious deposit.
Rehydrate and fix samples by immersing them in 20% diluted acetic acid for 48 hours.
Obtain a solution containing two phases: a liquid phase with DCD in suspension and a solid-phase slope.
Centrifuge 200 μL of the supernatant from the suspended DCD at 800 turns per minute for 10 minutes.
Prepare two spots per slide using the centrifuged material.
Produce four slides per sample: two slides are colored with Papanicolaou technique after fixing with lacquer.
The other two slides are colored using May–Grünwald–Giemsa (MGG) technique after air drying.
Centrifuge the remaining solid phase at 3500 rpm for 10 min.
Keep the supernatant in reserve for a later cytological study.
Recuperate the base of centrifugation and fix it for 24 h in AFA solution (acetic acid, formaldehyde, and alcohol).
Decalcify the sample after fixation.
Place the decalcified sample in a cassette on foam.
Proceed with dehydration in xylene followed by increasing alcohol baths.
Include the sample in liquid paraffin.
Cool the included sample.
Section the sample using a microtome to obtain slices of 6-10 μm thickness.
Deposit the sections on an albumenized slide and air-dry them freely.
Dewax the slides and rehydrate them by immersion in xylene followed by increasing alcohol baths down to distilled water.
Perform periodic acid Schiff (PAS) staining for each sample.
Carry out Gram staining for each sample.
Conduct toluidine blue staining for each sample.
Stain each sample with hematoxylin–eosin-saffron (HES).
